Multi-forge Priority Poker design (research + planning brief). PROBLEM: Priority Poker (ui-priority-poker/app.py + state.initiatives[].rank, used by Marshal as Priority Rule #3 in personas/marshal/CLAUDE.md) was designed for a single-Forge rig. With N=3 Forges + Assembly now live (validated 2026-04-17), five assumptions break: (1) single global rank means strict serial consumption — three top-ranked initiatives can't run in parallel even though three Forges are available; (2) no contention model — two top initiatives both touching cli.py guarantee Assembly rebase conflicts; (3) no parallelism semantics per initiative — some initiatives are inherently parallel-safe, others need to serialize; (4) no Forge affinity — forge-quench has built deep cli.py context across t-411/t-414/t-419/t-422 and round-robin loses that; (5) Assembly back-pressure invisible — if Assembly drain rate < dispatch rate, more pushes just create a backlog. DELIVERABLES — produce two files: (A) research/multi-forge-poker-design.md — ~2-3 page brief enumerating the five broken assumptions with concrete examples from the 2026-04-17 hardening sprint (e.g., t-423 forge-anneal/forge-quench duplicate work; t-425/t-423 Assembly rejections under load); enumerate the three design options (Lanes / Affinity-tagged single Poker / Two-layer Initiative+Task Poker) with pros/cons each; recommend the hybrid B+C-lite approach below; include UI sketches (drag-to-rank stays + per-initiative parallelism/affinity/touches chips). (B) plans/multi-forge-poker-plan.md — break the recommended approach into ~4 ordered implementation tasks ready for Marshal to dispatch. RECOMMENDED HYBRID (Anvil's framing 2026-04-17): (1) keep single global Poker ranking — human's main priority knob, unchanged; (2) add three fields per initiative: parallelism (serial|parallel, default parallel), affinity ([forge-id], default empty=any), touches ([path-glob], default empty=no contention claim, optionally auto-suggested from task descriptions); (3) Marshal's dispatch becomes a constraint walk — for each idle Forge, walk initiatives by rank, skip if parallelism=serial AND another forge is on it, skip if affinity is set AND this forge isn't in the list AND a listed forge is idle, skip if touches overlaps an in-flight task's touches AND parallelism=serial, then find top unblocked task in initiative and dispatch; (4) Assembly back-pressure — if .assembly-queue.jsonl depth >= 2 * N_forges, Marshal pauses dispatching new work, services in-flight only. PRESERVES: human still does drag-to-rank; the three new fields are advisory and default to today's behavior, so existing initiatives work unchanged. ENABLES: real N=3 throughput on parallel-friendly initiatives, automatic serialization where needed, forge-context preservation, Assembly-aware throttling. SCOPE FOR THIS TASK: research + planning only. ~2 heats. Implementation tasks (schema additions, Marshal constraint walk, Poker UI extensions, back-pressure logic) get filed by the planning doc as separate t-XXX entries. Clean Forge worktree on heat-reject so WIP pollution does not compound. ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-04-18): when pre-submit pytest gate (t-427) rejects, Forge does not commit (correct), but working-tree modifications stay on disk. Next heat starts: start-heat creates a new per-task branch off main, but pending modifications from the rejected heat PROPAGATE (git checkout does not discard modified-but-unstaged files). pytest on the new task runs against stale code, fails, rejects again, pollution compounds. Observed across t-425, t-426, t-431 — 3-4 consecutive rejects each, each against a progressively more polluted worktree. Fresh /tmp worktree reproduction passed because zero pollution. WHAT: heat-reject path must leave the worktree clean. Three candidate designs: (A) Reset-on-reject — end-heats reject branch calls git reset --hard <branch-point> + git clean -fdx before returning. Simplest. (B) Stash-before-tests — pre-submit gate stashes, runs pytest, pops on pass or drops on reject. Heavier. (C) Reset-on-start — start-heat asserts clean working tree and resets if not. RECOMMEND A plus a start-heat assertion that warns + resets if working tree is not clean. TESTS: simulate rejected heat, assert worktree clean after reject. ACCEPTANCE: t-425/t-426/t-431 retried on this fix must not repro the thrash. Anvil-filed 2026-04-18 after manual reset of 3 forge worktrees unblocked the hardening sprint.

Within an hour, state.json showed used=824 — a 79-heat decrease without any rollback directive. Suspects: (a) smithy sync-stages recomputing used from stage-heat sums (sums were 892 pre-reconcile), (b) a Forge worktree writing stale snapshot back despite t-419, (c) patrol --fix reversing the reconcile, (d) Marshal session writing cached in-memory value. Method: bisect the git log for state.json writes between commits 64eedda and 1c7f84f, cross-ref with rig-events.jsonl and nudge-queue timestamps to identify the writer. Output: research/budget-drift-rca.md with reproduction steps + recommended fix (likely: make budget.used monotonic-or-explicit-override in state code; or remove any recomputation path that competes with worklog-as-truth).
queue.priority_reason: trust-in-record bug; drifting budget undermines every downstream metric (ini-019 depends on this being fixed)

queue.desc: BLOCKER — fix _do_assembly_reject TypeError. Location: smithy/smithy/cli.py:826-827. Code: hp = task.get("human_priority") or 0; task["human_priority"] = hp + 5. Fails when human_priority is a string like "p1"/"p2" (which Anvil started assigning on new tasks). Fix: normalize human_priority in one place — accept int, "N", or "pN" forms; store as int internally; raise TypeError fixed. Add tests: (a) integer input, (b) "p1" string input, (c) None input, (d) assembly-reject bumps priority correctly for each form. Check all other callsites that read/write human_priority and align them. Root cause note: Anvil introduced "p1"/"p2" strings on t-444..t-454; pre-existing queue used ints. This is the collision.

BLOCKER — decouple Assembly rebase from the Forge worktree. Current bug: rebase_forge_branch (smithy/smithy/assembly.py:40-59) runs `git rebase` in the Forge's worktree, which rebases WHATEVER branch is currently checked out there — not the per-task branch being merged. Fails when Forge has moved on to a new task, and fails 'unstaged changes' when Forge is mid-heat with dirty worktree. The right architecture: Assembly must operate in its OWN workspace and reference branches by name, not by worktree checkout. Design: (a) Add ensure_staging_worktree(project_dir) that creates/reuses .worktrees/_assembly-staging. (b) Replace rebase_forge_branch(project_dir, forge_id) with rebase_task_branch(project_dir, forge_id, task_id) that does: `git -C staging checkout -B _merge-<task-id> <forge-id>/<task-id>` (snapshot ref), then `git -C staging rebase main`. Returns the staging ref name on clean, or conflict/error dict as today. (c) Update ff_merge_forge_branch to accept a source_ref parameter (defaults to <forge-id>/<task-id> for back-compat), so Assembly merges FROM the rebased staging ref into main in project_dir as before. (d) On success, cleanup the original <forge-id>/<task-id> branch (Forge has moved on — already validated by t-420 per-task branches). (e) Update all cli.py callers (assembly_tick, any test harness) to pass task_id. Properties to preserve: Forge NEVER waits for Assembly — once it submits, it's free to queue-pop the next task. Branch refs in git worktree setups are shared across worktrees, so the staging approach works without additional sync. Tests: (1) Forge on the branch clean, (2) Forge on a DIFFERENT branch clean, (3) Forge on different branch DIRTY, (4) concurrent: Forge commits t-460 while Assembly merges t-455, (5) rebase conflict path still returns {status:conflict, files:[...]}. Reverts the earlier bad 'Forge stays on branch' workaround — the whole point is Forge throughput must not block on Assembly.
queue.priority_reason: assembly rejected: tests failed: ERROR t

queue.desc: FOLLOW-UP to t-456: complete the staging-worktree decoupling. Current t-456 fix (rebase_forge_branch does checkout+stash in Forge worktree) is partial — eliminates the wrong-branch class but still races with active Forges when Forge writes fresh files between stash and rebase. Observed 2026-04-18 drain: 2 unstaged-changes rejects on t-443 and t-442 (both forge-anneal submits whose Forge was mid-heat at drain time). Real fix: Assembly operates in its OWN worktree .worktrees/_assembly-staging, never touches Forge worktrees. Per the original t-456 design: (a) ensure_staging_worktree(project_dir) creates/reuses the Assembly worktree, (b) snapshot the task branch into _merge-<task-id> via checkout -B, (c) rebase + run tests in staging, (d) ff-merge from the staging ref in project_dir, (e) cleanup temp ref + delete source task branch. Keep the existing rebase_forge_branch for back-compat; add rebase_task_branch as the new primary. Update assembly_tick callers. Tests: concurrent case (Forge writing to its worktree while Assembly merges), clean case, conflict case, stale-branch case.
queue.priority_reason: eliminates the Assembly-Forge worktree race class (2 of 6 drain rejects)

queue.desc: Eliminate MEMORY.md merge conflicts between parallel Forges. Current: personas/forge/memory/MEMORY.md is shared by all 3 Forges; concurrent edits on separate per-task branches produce severe conflicts Assembly rejects (3 rejects in 2026-04-18 drain: t-431×2 and t-441). Design options: (a) per-forge memory subdirs personas/forge/memory/quench/ temper/ anneal/ — eliminates collision, each Forge writes its own file; OR (b) append-only memory log with forge-id + timestamp per entry, later consolidation job. Recommend (a) — simpler, clear ownership, natural git semantics. Migration: move existing personas/forge/memory/*.md into quench/ subdir (most recent edits), leave others empty, update forge CLAUDE.md path references. Add patrol check that flags divergence between subdirs to catch drift.

queue.desc: Add patrol check for Assembly-Forge worktree contention. After the staging-worktree decoupling lands, we still want a lightweight check that Assembly never enters a Forge worktree for merge ops (to catch regressions). Audit all callers of _worktree() in assembly.py and cli.py; verify assembly-tick path only touches the staging worktree for rebase/test. Document the rule in assembly.py docstring and CLAUDE.md. Output: scripts/check-assembly-isolation or patrol check #11.

Pin smithy editable install to main, never a worktree. Root cause observed 2026-04-18: the global editable install (pip install -e smithy/) had been last run from a worktree (forge-quench/smithy/), so every pane imported from that stale tree. When Assembly ran pytest inside any worktree, collection of tests imported from main (e.g., test_t455_normalize_hp.py requiring normalize_human_priority) failed because the stale install lacked the symbol. 3 rejects hit this pattern (t-447 + two earlier transients). Assembly unstuck by re-binding to main. Fix: (a) add post-Assembly-merge hook that runs pip install -e from main-repo smithy/ whenever smithy code changes (detect via merge-commit paths); OR (b) guard in smithy startup that warns if __file__ is inside .worktrees/; OR (c) refactor so every pane uses a PYTHONPATH prepend to main-repo smithy/ and editable install is frozen to main. Recommend (a)+(b) — automated rebind post-merge, plus a loud warning when detection fails. Tests: regression test for module path invariant; e2e smoke that a merge touching smithy/ triggers rebind.

initiatives.title: Parallel Forges
initiatives.description: Run multiple Forge workers concurrently via per-Forge git worktrees. Dedicated Assembly teammate handles merge queue integration (conflicts, test-on-integrate, merge ordering). Unlocks parallelism (Marshal dispatches N heats simultaneously) and enforces branch hygiene. Incremental: N=2 proof before N=3+.

initiatives.title: Forge Observability
initiatives.description: Read-only aggregation layer over worklog.tsv + rig-events.jsonl + assembly-log.jsonl + state.json + git log. Three surfaces: (L0) smithy report CLI — initiative burn-down, forge idle%, top failure buckets. (L1) Bellows Forge Ops dashboard — initiative panel with burn bars, task drill-down with timeline, persona heatmap, Issues view (ghost submits, test recurrence, Assembly rejects, thrash ≥3 retries), flow diagram. (L2) per-heat JSON snapshots for time-series regression analysis. Principle: no new write paths; deterministic replay from the record. Pre-req: retro-annotate task→initiative_id mapping (schema gap in state.queue).

initiatives.title: Batched Assembly with Bisect-on-Fail
initiatives.description: Gas Town Refinery pattern adapted for Assembly: batch N pending submissions into one integration branch, run full test suite ONCE, fast-forward-merge all on green, git-bisect to isolate breaker on red. Amortizes test cost across parallel submissions; log2(N) fault isolation replaces whole-batch rejection. Data (2026-04-18): current Assembly merge latency median 1.0min/p90 1.12min — merge speed is not the issue. Real cost is rejection thrash: 50%% reject rate (16/32 events), concentrated in 4 tasks, 14/16 from test failures. Batch+bisect pays off at N>=3 concurrent submits. Does NOT address Assembly-env bug (t-431/t-426 class) — orthogonal fix needed. v1 scope: count-or-time batch window (>=2 submits OR 60s), sequential rebase within batch, standard git bisect run with smithy test shim.

initiatives.title: Context Reset Per Task (Forge)
initiatives.description: Hypothesis: Forge session context between tasks is not load-bearing — every durable output (code, state, worklog, memory, checkpoint) already persists on disk. Cross-task context accumulation causes pollution (stale branch name in prompt, autoregressive drift) and unnecessary token burn. v1 design: Claude Code hook on clean end-heat triggers /clear; persona re-loads via system prompt + CLAUDE.md + persona memory on next turn. Clear only on clean end-heat (complete/submit), NOT on partial/blocked/rejected — partials preserve debug trail. Depends on ini-019 telemetry to measure win (context tokens at end-heat, rejection rate before/after). A/B validation plan: one forge with auto-clear, one without, ~20 heats each, compare value scores + rejection rate + rework frequency.

initiatives.title: Queue Cockpit
initiatives.description: Primary UI surface for steering per-task prioritization. Live view of the actual task queue synced to state.json, showing every task with Marshal priority, human priority, stage, status, priority reason, initiative tag. Human downranks/promotes/pins/defers from this surface. Poker remains for initiative-level steering; this is the per-task master cockpit.
initiatives.intent: Give the human a way to ensure that individual task assignments conform to the high-level intent the human has, and gives a way to identify and correct drift.

initiatives.title: Intents as Primitives
initiatives.description: Intent is a primitive field attached uniformly to every unit of work (task, initiative, project). Same shape everywhere — no 'level' concept in storage. Inheritance/chain is one view over intents, not the core concept. Other views: search by intent content, gap audit (units with no intent), drift detection (contradicting intents). Auto-discoverable per-unit AND inline-editable wherever a unit is displayed.

initiatives.title: Steering patterns research
initiatives.description: Research how humans steer autonomous systems — not monitor, STEER. The core question: what controls does a human need to change direction without becoming a bottleneck? Study: (1) Real-time strategy games (StarCraft command hierarchy — strategic goals, tactical orders, unit autonomy), (2) Military C2 frameworks (mission-type orders, commander's intent, OODA), (3) Product management (OKRs, roadmap prioritization, sprint planning), (4) Air traffic control (constraints not commands), (5) Existing AI tools (Devin's chat-to-steer, Cursor's accept/reject, Claude Code hooks). For each, extract: what decisions the human makes, at what frequency, what information they need to decide, and what the feedback loop looks like. Deliverable: research/steering-patterns.md with a taxonomy of steering modes and which are worth prototyping as UIs.

initiatives.title: UI A: Priority poker
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI where the human steers by ranking, not approving. Shows all active initiatives as cards. Human drags to reorder — that IS the steering. No approve/reject buttons. Everything proposed is fair game unless explicitly killed. The ranking determines allocation weight. Top card gets 3x budget share, second gets 2x, rest get 1x. Real-time: as Forge works, cards show live progress and the stack rebalances. The human's only job: keep the stack in the right order. Inspired by planning poker + priority queues. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.

initiatives.title: Marshal agent
initiatives.description: New persona sitting between Anvil and Forge. An AI agent (Claude session) that runs before every heat and decides task ordering. Replaces the wavefront allocator. Reads all steering signals: theme rankings, initiative status/budget caps, constraint board rules, priority poker order, timeline allocations, task priorities, blocked_by deps, recent worklog history, human_priorities. Produces a single ordered list of next N tasks written to state.json. Forge becomes a pure executor — reads the list, pops the top task, does the work. The Marshal makes the steering UIs meaningful: they're all inputs that the Marshal synthesizes into one queue. Architecture: Anvil (strategy) → Marshal (ordering) → Forge (execution).

initiatives.title: UI reactivity — state change detection
initiatives.description: All 4 steering UIs should reflect state.json changes without auto-polling. Options: (1) Manual refresh button visible on every UI — 'Refresh' button in header that reloads data via AJAX (not full page reload). (2) File watcher via SSE — backend watches state.json with watchdog/inotify and pushes events to frontend via Server-Sent Events. Frontend updates DOM on event. (3) Hybrid — manual refresh button always visible, plus optional SSE for live updates. Start with manual refresh button on all 4 UIs (simplest, no dependencies). Then add SSE as an enhancement. Each UI needs: a GET /api/state endpoint returning current data as JSON, a JS function that fetches it and re-renders the relevant DOM elements, a visible Refresh button in the header that calls this function.

initiatives.title: UI C: Timeline view
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI where the human steers by shaping a timeline. Horizontal axis is heats (or time). Initiatives are horizontal bars showing planned start/end. The human drags bar endpoints to allocate budget. Overlapping bars = parallel work. Gaps = cool-down. The visual makes tradeoffs obvious — stretching one initiative squeezes another. Forge reads the timeline and works accordingly. Inspired by Gantt charts but interactive and simple. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.
initiatives.intent: Play with different UIs which would inform a good way of adopting steerability.

initiatives.title: Logic Subject Expansion
initiatives.description: Add more topics and exercises to Logic & Critical Thinking

initiatives.title: UI D: Intent editor
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI focused on natural-language steering. The human writes a short intent statement (2-3 sentences). The system decomposes it into themes, initiatives, and tasks automatically. Human reviews the decomposition and edits — delete a branch, promote a task, add a constraint. The intent is the source of truth, not the task list. When intent changes, the decomposition updates. Inspired by commander's intent in military doctrine. The human thinks in outcomes, the system thinks in tasks. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.

initiatives.title: UI B: Constraint board
initiatives.description: A desktop web UI where the human steers by setting constraints, not giving orders. Instead of telling Forge what to do, the human defines boundaries: 'no more than 5 heats on research', 'testing must stay above 80%', 'don't touch tutor', 'ship something deployable by Friday'. Constraints are cards on a board. Forge works freely within them. When a constraint would be violated, Forge stops and asks. The human's only job: add/remove/adjust constraints. Inspired by air traffic control — direct through boundaries, not waypoints. Build as a standalone page in Bellows.

initiatives.title: Collaboration patterns landscape
initiatives.description: Research how humans and AI agents collaborate effectively. Survey existing frameworks: OODA loops, PDCA, delegation matrices, trust calibration, oversight gradients (from full autonomy to pair programming). Study real systems: Devin, Cursor, Codex, aider, Claude Code, GPT-Pilot. Identify patterns that Smithy doesn't use yet. Deliverable: research/collaboration-patterns.md with a taxonomy of collaboration modes and recommendations for which to prototype.

initiatives.title: Async handoff protocols
initiatives.description: Research and design better async handoff between human and AI. Current model: inbox.md/outbox.md + dispatch files. Problems: context loss between sessions, no structured status requests, human has to read raw files. Explore: structured status requests (human asks a question, gets an answer next heat), decision queues with deadlines, progress summaries that compress intelligently, proactive alerts (not just outbox dumps). Deliverable: research doc + design for improved async protocol.

initiatives.title: Trust and autonomy calibration
initiatives.description: Research how to dynamically adjust AI autonomy based on track record. Currently Forge has fixed autonomy (full within budget). Explore: earned autonomy (start supervised, earn independence), risk-based gating (low-risk tasks auto-approved, high-risk need human), confidence signals (AI reports its own uncertainty, human decides when to intervene), learning from corrections (human corrects, AI adjusts future behavior). Deliverable: research doc + design for adaptive autonomy.

initiatives.title: Terminal dashboard (Rich)
initiatives.description: Build a terminal-based dashboard using Python Rich library. Real-time view of Forge state without leaving the terminal. Shows: budget bar, stage progress (colored bars), current heat, last 5 worklog entries, pending tasks, initiative board (compact). Single command: 'smithy dashboard' that refreshes on file changes (watchdog or polling). Complements Bellows — Bellows for steering, terminal for monitoring while Forge runs.

initiatives.title: Slack/Discord bot interface
initiatives.description: Build a bot that bridges Forge to a messaging platform. Human sends messages in Slack/Discord, they appear in inbox.md. Forge outbox updates post to a channel. Decision cards become interactive messages with approve/defer/reject buttons. Status requests return formatted summaries. Start with one platform (likely Discord — free, good bot API). Lightweight: just a bridge, not a replacement for Bellows.

initiatives.title: Email digest
initiatives.description: Build an email digest that summarizes Forge activity. Daily or per-run summary sent via email (or written to a file for manual sending). Contains: heats completed, stage progress deltas, decisions needing attention, notable events (yellows/reds), link to Bellows. Template-based (Jinja2). Could also serve as the foundation for a webhook/notification system.

initiatives.title: Mobile-first Bellows redesign
initiatives.description: Redesign Bellows for phone-first use. Current Bellows is desktop-oriented. The human checks status from their phone more than laptop. Key screens: (1) project list with signal dots — one glance, (2) initiative approval — swipe to approve/reject, (3) status summary — compact, no scrolling needed. CSS-only responsive or a separate mobile template. PWA with push notifications for decisions.

intents.text: Create an AI collaborator who can run autonomously, while also being responsive to human steers, and can carry out the high-level intents that the human expresses and wants.
Give the human a way to ensure that individual task assignments conform to the high-level intent the human has, and gives a way to identify and correct drift.
Play with different UIs which would inform a good way of adopting steerability.
